decision_conditions: The proposal would result in the loss of an existing family-sized dwellinghouse (Use Class C3) for which there is an identified need within the Borough and its replacement with a House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4). Furthermore, by reason of the occupation of the property by six unrelated individuals, the proposal would result in an over-intensive form of residential occupation, giving rise to increased levels of noise, disturbance, comings and goings, visitor activity, deliveries and vehicular movements, particularly having regard to the site's constrained access arrangements and relationship with neighbouring residential properties. The proposal would therefore fail to safeguard the Borough's housing stock and would be detrimental to the residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers. The development is consequently contrary to Policies DMH1, DMH2, DMH5 and DMHB11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H10 and Policy D3 of the L

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would provide safe and suitable access arrangements or policy-compliant vehicle and cycle parking facilities. The proposal would provide six car parking spaces, significantly exceeding the Council's adopted parking standard for a six-person HMO, whilst failing to provide compliant cycle parking and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Furthermore, insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that vehicles can safely access, manoeuvre within and egress the site via the constrained access arrangements. The proposal would therefore be detrimental to highway and pedestrian safety and would fail to promote sustainable transport objectives, contrary to Policy TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies T2, T4, T5 and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT1, DMT2, DMT5 and DMT6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposal would fail to provide an acceptable standard of living accommodation for future occupiers by reason of the provision of substandard bedroom accommodation, inadequate sanitary facilities, the poor quality and uncertain status of the ground floor studio accommodation, and the absence of adequate and functional private external amenity space. The development would therefore provide a poor standard of residential environment for future occupiers and is contrary to Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMHB16 and DMHB18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

We have however been unable to seek solutions to problems arising from the application as the principal of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
description: Change of use from dwellinghouse (Class C3) to small house in multiple occupation HMO for up to 6 persons (Class C4) (Retrospective)
